records.literal_gloss: Praise Yah! Praise, my soul, YHWH.

en.L: Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}! Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, my soul!
en.B: Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}! My soul, praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}!
en.R: Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}! With all that I am, I praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

fr.L: Louez {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yah}} ! Loue {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, mon âme !
fr.B: Louez {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yah}} ! Mon âme, loue {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} !
fr.R: Louez {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yah}} ! De tout mon être, je loue {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.

decisions.choice: Praise Yah: hallelu-yah, a call to praise the LORD
decisions.reason: The words (hallelu yah) are a command to a group, "praise Yah"; Yah is the short form of the divine name (YHWH). Psalms 146-150 each open and close with this call. Here in Psalm 146 the renderings translate it, as "Praise the LORD", rather than keep it as the borrowed word "Hallelujah".

decisions.choice: Psalms 146-150: the closing songs of praise
decisions.reason: The last five psalms each begin and end with "Praise Yah". Together they close the book of Psalms with praise, moving from one voice (146:1-2) to every creature (148; 150:6). They have long been sung every morning in Jewish prayer.

decisions.choice: my soul: my whole self
decisions.reason: The psalmist speaks to himself, calling his whole being (nefesh) to praise, as in 103:1 and 104:1.

decisions.choice: With all that I am, I praise the LORD
decisions.reason: As in 103:1, Readable says what it means to call on one's own soul.

decisions.choice: "Mon âme" kept at Balanced, as the English Balanced keeps "My soul"; "De tout mon être" at Readable
decisions.reason: The psalmist speaks to himself; the address "mon âme" is clear French for this, so Balanced keeps it, and Readable says what it means.

source.text: אֲהַלְלָ֣ה יְהוָ֣ה בְּחַיָּ֑י אֲזַמְּרָ֖ה לֵֽאלֹהַ֣י בְּעוֹדִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: I will praise YHWH in my life; I will sing praises to my God in my yet.

en.L: I will praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in my life; I will sing praises to my God while I [still] am.
en.B: All my life I will praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; as long as I exist I will make music for my God.
en.R: I will praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} my whole life long. I will sing to my God for as long as I am alive.

fr.L: Je louerai {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dans ma vie ; je chanterai pour mon Dieu tant que je [serai] encore.
fr.B: Toute ma vie je louerai {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ; tant que j’existerai, je jouerai pour mon Dieu.
fr.R: Je louerai {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} toute ma vie. Je chanterai pour mon Dieu aussi longtemps que je vivrai.

decisions.reason: The same vow, in nearly the same words, closes Psalm 104 (104:33).

decisions.choice: while I yet am: as long as I live
decisions.reason: The phrase (be'odi, "in my still") means as long as I go on living.

decisions.choice: sing praises: make music in praise
decisions.reason: The verb (zamar) is singing, often with instruments (33:2).

records.literal_gloss: Do not trust in nobles, in a son of humankind, who there is not for him deliverance.

en.L: Do not trust in nobles, in {{gender:a human being|a son of man}}, in whom [there is] no deliverance.
en.B: Do not rely on rulers, on mere mortals, who have no power to rescue.
en.R: Do not trust powerful leaders or any other human being. No person can really rescue anyone.

fr.L: Ne vous confiez pas dans les nobles, dans {{gender:un être humain|un fils d’homme}}, en qui [il n’y a] pas de délivrance.
fr.B: Ne comptez pas sur les grands, sur de simples mortels, qui n’ont pas le pouvoir de sauver.
fr.R: N’ayez pas confiance dans les chefs puissants ni dans aucun autre être humain. Personne ne peut vraiment sauver quelqu’un.

decisions.choice: nobles: powerful people, princes
decisions.reason: The word (nedivim) is people of rank and influence (118:9; 113:8).

decisions.choice: a son of humankind: a mere human
decisions.reason: "Son of adam" is any human being (8:5). The word adam echoes the word for the ground (adamah) to which he returns in verse 4 (Genesis 2:7; 3:19).

decisions.choice: who has no deliverance: who cannot save
decisions.reason: The words say that no deliverance (teshu'ah) is to be found with this person: they cannot rescue others, and in the end cannot rescue themselves (verse 4).

decisions.choice: mere mortals (B); any other human being (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew singular stands for anyone at all. Balanced makes it plural, which includes men and women alike; Readable says "any human being". Literal keeps the singular, with the traditional wording as a setting.

decisions.choice: "un être humain" by default, "un fils d'homme" as the gender alternative, at Literal; the pronouns of verse 4 ("son", "il") take none
alternatives: a setting on each pronoun, as the English Literal has
decisions.reason: Ben ʾadam means a mere human. French puts the setting on the noun; both options are masculine, so "son souffle" and "il retourne" in verse 4 fit either, and need no setting of their own.

source.text: תֵּצֵ֣א ר֭וּחוֹ יָשֻׁ֣ב לְאַדְמָת֑וֹ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַ֝ה֗וּא אָבְד֥וּ עֶשְׁתֹּנֹתָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: His breath goes out; he returns to his ground; in that day his plans perish.

en.L: {{gender:Their|His}} breath goes out, {{gender:they return|he returns}} to {{gender:their|his}} ground; on that day {{gender:their|his}} plans perish.
en.B: Their breath leaves them and they go back to the soil they came from; that same day all they had planned is gone.
en.R: When they breathe their last, their bodies go back to the dust. On that day all their plans come to an end.

fr.L: Son souffle s’en va, il retourne à sa terre ; en ce jour-là ses projets périssent.
fr.B: Leur souffle les quitte et ils retournent à la terre d’où ils viennent ; ce jour-là, tout ce qu’ils avaient prévu disparaît.
fr.R: Quand ils rendent leur dernier souffle, leur corps retourne à la poussière. Ce jour-là, tous leurs projets prennent fin.

decisions.choice: breath: the breath of life
decisions.reason: The word (ruach) is breath, wind or spirit. When it goes out, life ends (104:29).

decisions.choice: he returns to his ground: he dies and turns to dust
decisions.reason: "His ground" is the earth he was taken from (Genesis 3:19).

decisions.choice: plans: thoughts, schemes
decisions.reason: The word ('eshtonot) is found only here in the Bible; it comes from a verb for thinking, and means the plans and ideas of a ruler or anyone else.

decisions.choice: the soil they came from (B); the dust (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "his ground" means (m2).

source.text: אַשְׁרֵ֗י שֶׁ֤אֵ֣ל יַעֲקֹ֣ב בְּעֶזְר֑וֹ שִׂ֝בְר֗וֹ עַל־יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: How blessed [is he] who the God of Jacob [is] in his help, his hope [is] on YHWH his God.

en.L: How blessed [is the one] whose help [is] the God of Jacob, whose hope [is] on {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} {{gender:their|his}} God!
en.B: How blessed are those who have the God of Jacob to help them, whose hope rests on {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God!
en.R: Life is truly good for people whose helper is the God of Jacob. They put their hope in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God.

fr.L: Heureux [celui] dont le secours [est] le Dieu de Jacob, dont l’espoir [est] {{divine_name:dans le SEIGNEUR|en Yahvé}} son Dieu !
fr.B: Heureux ceux qui ont le Dieu de Jacob pour les secourir, et dont l’espoir repose sur {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} leur Dieu !
fr.R: La vie est vraiment belle pour ceux qui ont le Dieu de Jacob pour les aider. Ils mettent leur espoir dans {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} leur Dieu.

decisions.choice: How blessed: a life that goes well
decisions.reason: The exclamation ('ashre) of 1:1. The one who leans on God is better off than the one who leans on rulers (verse 3).

decisions.choice: the God of Jacob: the God of Israel
decisions.reason: Jacob, who was renamed Israel, stands for the people descended from him; this is the God who kept faith with their ancestor (46:8).

decisions.choice: in his help: as his help
decisions.reason: The small word "in" here marks what something is: the God of Jacob is his help.

decisions.choice: Life is truly good for
decisions.reason: As in 1:1, Readable says what the exclamation ('ashre) means.

decisions.choice: those ... their
decisions.reason: The Hebrew speaks of one person, standing for anyone who trusts God. Balanced and Readable make it plural, which includes men and women alike.

source.text: עֹשֶׂ֤ה׀שָׁ֘מַ֤יִם וָאָ֗רֶץ אֶת־הַיָּ֥ם וְאֶת־כָּל־אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֑ם הַשֹּׁמֵ֖ר אֱמֶ֣ת לְעוֹלָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: making heaven and earth, the sea and all that [is] in them, the one keeping faithfulness forever,

en.L: who made heaven and earth, the sea and all that [is] in them, who keeps faithfulness forever,
en.B: who made heaven and earth and the sea with all they contain, who remains true forever,
en.R: He made the sky, the earth and the sea, and all that fills them. He stays faithful forever.

fr.L: qui a fait le ciel et la terre, la mer et tout ce qui [est] en eux, qui garde la fidélité pour toujours,
fr.B: qui a fait le ciel, la terre et la mer avec tout ce qu’ils contiennent, qui reste fidèle pour toujours,
fr.R: Il a fait le ciel, la terre et la mer, et tout ce qui les remplit. Il reste fidèle pour toujours.

decisions.reason: The words echo the commandment about the Sabbath (Exodus 20:11). The believers in Jerusalem pray to God in these words (Acts 4:24), and Paul and Barnabas use them in Lystra (Acts 14:15).

decisions.choice: faithfulness: keeping faith, being true
decisions.reason: The word ('emet) is truth and also faithfulness; here it is God keeping his word, unlike the rulers of verses 3-4.

decisions.choice: a sentence that runs on
decisions.reason: Verses 6-7 go on describing "the LORD his God" of verse 5, so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

decisions.choice: He
decisions.reason: Readable starts new sentences and says who made all this.

source.text: עֹשֶׂ֤ה מִשְׁפָּ֨ט׀לָעֲשׁוּקִ֗ים נֹתֵ֣ן לֶ֭חֶם לָרְעֵבִ֑ים יְ֝הוָ֗ה מַתִּ֥יר אֲסוּרִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: doing justice for the oppressed, giving bread to the hungry. YHWH sets free prisoners.

en.L: who does justice for the oppressed, who gives bread to the hungry. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} sets prisoners free;
en.B: who brings justice to the oppressed and provides bread for the hungry. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} releases the prisoners;
en.R: He makes things right for people who are treated unfairly. He gives food to hungry people. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} sets prisoners free.

fr.L: qui fait justice aux opprimés, qui donne du pain aux affamés. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} délie les prisonniers ;
fr.B: qui rend justice aux opprimés et donne du pain à ceux qui ont faim. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} libère les prisonniers ;
fr.R: Il remet les choses en ordre pour les gens qu’on traite injustement. Il donne à manger à ceux qui ont faim. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} libère les prisonniers.

decisions.choice: justice: putting right what is wrong
decisions.reason: To do justice (mishpat) for the oppressed is to take their side and set right the wrong done to them (103:6).

decisions.choice: five lines that begin with the LORD
decisions.reason: From here to verse 9 the name YHWH begins five short lines in a row, each naming one thing the LORD does for those who have no one else.

decisions.choice: sets free: unties, releases
decisions.reason: The verb (hittir) is to loosen bonds, used of prisoners set free (105:20).

source.text: יְהוָ֤ה׀פֹּ֘קֵ֤חַ עִוְרִ֗ים יְ֭הוָה זֹקֵ֣ף כְּפוּפִ֑ים יְ֝הוָ֗ה אֹהֵ֥ב צַדִּיקִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: YHWH opens [the] blind; YHWH raises up [the] bowed down; YHWH loves [the] righteous.

en.L: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} opens [the eyes of the] blind; {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} raises up [those who are] bowed down; {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} loves [the] righteous;
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} makes the blind see; {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} raises up those bent low; {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} loves people who are righteous;
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} helps blind people see. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} lifts up people who are weighed down. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} loves people who do what is right.

fr.L: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ouvre [les yeux des] aveugles ; {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} redresse [ceux qui sont] courbés ; {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} aime [les] justes ;
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} rend la vue aux aveugles ; {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} redresse ceux qui sont courbés ; {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} aime les justes ;
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} aide les aveugles à voir. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} relève les gens écrasés par leurs malheurs. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} aime les gens qui font ce qui est bien.

decisions.choice: opens the blind: opens the eyes of the blind
decisions.reason: The verb (paqach) is used for opening eyes; the hope that the LORD would open blind eyes is in Isaiah 35:5 and 42:7.

decisions.choice: the bowed down: people bent low
people who do what is right
decisions.reason: As in the earlier psalms, Readable says what the righteous (tsaddiqim) are.

source.text: יְהוָ֤ה׀שֹׁ֘מֵ֤ר אֶת־גֵּרִ֗ים יָת֣וֹם וְאַלְמָנָ֣ה יְעוֹדֵ֑ד וְדֶ֖רֶךְ רְשָׁעִ֣ים יְעַוֵּֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: YHWH watches over sojourners; fatherless and widow he relieves, and [the] way of [the] wicked he makes crooked.

en.L: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} watches over sojourners; [the] fatherless and widow {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} relieves, but [the] way of [the] wicked {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} makes crooked.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} protects the foreigners living in the land; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} upholds the orphan and the widow, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} overturns the way of the wicked.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} protects foreigners. He takes care of orphans and widows. But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} ruins the plans of wicked people.

fr.L: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} garde les immigrés ; [l’]orphelin et [la] veuve, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les soutient, mais [le] chemin des méchants, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} le tord.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} protège les étrangers qui vivent dans le pays ; {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} soutient l’orphelin et la veuve, mais {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} renverse le chemin des méchants.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} protège les étrangers. Il prend soin des orphelins et des veuves. Mais {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} fait échouer les projets des méchants.

decisions.choice: sojourners, the fatherless and the widow: people with no one to protect them
decisions.reason: Foreigners living in Israel (gerim) owned no land, and orphans and widows had no man of the family to stand up for them. The law names them again and again as people God himself protects (Deuteronomy 10:18; 24:17).

decisions.choice: relieves: helps up, sustains
decisions.reason: The verb ('oded) is to restore or hold up (147:6).

decisions.choice: makes crooked: bends so that it leads to ruin
decisions.reason: The verb ('iwwet) is to twist or bend. The way of the wicked is bent until it ends nowhere (1:6).

decisions.choice: ruins the plans
decisions.reason: Readable says what it means to bend someone's way (m3).

decisions.choice: "les immigrés" at Literal for gerim; "les étrangers" at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: A ger is a foreigner who has settled in the land without family or rights there. The Pentateuch terms give "l'étranger, l'immigré"; Literal uses "immigrés" to show that they live in the land, which Balanced says in a phrase.

source.text: יִמְלֹ֤ךְ יְהוָ֨ה׀לְעוֹלָ֗ם אֱלֹהַ֣יִךְ צִ֭יּוֹן לְדֹ֥ר וָדֹ֗ר הַֽלְלוּ־יָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: YHWH will reign forever, your God, Zion, to generation and generation. Praise Yah!

en.L: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will reign forever, your God, Zion, to generation and generation. Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}!
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will rule as King forever; Zion, your God will reign from one generation to the next. Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}!
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will be King forever! People of Zion, your God will rule for all time to come. Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}!

fr.L: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} régnera pour toujours, ton Dieu, Sion, de génération en génération. Louez {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yah}} !
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} régnera comme Roi pour toujours ; Sion, ton Dieu règnera d’une génération à l’autre. Louez {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yah}} !
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} sera Roi pour toujours ! Peuple de Sion, ton Dieu régnera pour tous les temps à venir. Louez {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yah}} !

decisions.choice: Exodus 15:18
decisions.reason: The song at the Red Sea ends with "the LORD will reign forever and ever" (Exodus 15:18). The King who rescued Israel rules for all time, unlike the rulers of verses 3-4.

decisions.choice: Zion: Jerusalem and its people
decisions.reason: Zion, the hill of the temple, stands for Jerusalem and for God's people.

decisions.choice: People of Zion
decisions.reason: Readable says that the city's people are addressed.
